messages.content: Explain why Earth has seasons. Answer in two to four sentences of plain prose.

message.content: Earth has seasons because its axis is tilted as it orbits the Sun. Throughout the year, this tilt causes different parts of the planet to lean either toward or away from the Sun. The hemisphere leaning toward the Sun receives more direct sunlight and experiences summer, while the hemisphere leaning away receives less direct sunlight and experiences winter.
